title: Junction-free polarity-tunable superconducting diode effect enables XNOR logic operation
abstract: The realization of the superconducting diode effect (SDE), characterized by non-reciprocal supercurrent, is a major step towards dissipationless logic circuits. A polarity-tunable superconducting diode with high diode efficiency primarily consists of Josephson-junction architectures that couple two superconducting regions via a weak link. Realizing an SDE without a weak-link junction would reduce fabrication complexity, lower electrical noise, and minimize dependence on junction quality. Here, we report an all-vdW, highly efficient, junction-free SDE in NbSe2, enabled by proximity-induced symmetry breaking from a strong uniaxial ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2 (F3GT). Superconducting diode efficiency of up to 30% is achieved at a small magnetic field of 50 mT. A field-free diode rectification effect is realized with diode polarity that is tunable by the F3GT spin polarization. Furthermore, by employing the active-field dependence of the SDE, a two-input exclusive-NOR (XNOR) logic gate operation is demonstrated. The findings highlight the potential utilization of magnetic proximity effect towards realizing junction-free superconducting diodes for high-performance, energy-efficient logic circuits.
summary: This paper reports the creation of a junction-free superconducting diode using a van der Waals heterostructure ($	ext{Fe}_3	ext{GeTe}_2/	ext{NbSe}_2$). By leveraging magnetic proximity effects, they achieve a highly efficient, polarity-tunable superconducting diode. This device is then successfully utilized to implement a two-input XNOR logic gate, marking a significant step toward superconducting logic circuits.
main_problem: The primary goal is to realize a superconducting diode effect (SDE) without the need for traditional, complex Josephson junctions to enable low-power, energy-efficient logic circuits.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated a highly efficient, junction-free SDE in an $	ext{NbSe}_2$ heterostructure, achieving up to 30% efficiency and enabling the operation of an XNOR logic gate.
method: The research involves fabricating and measuring transport properties ($	ext{V-I}$, $	ext{dV/dI}$, $	ext{R-T}$, $	ext{MR}$) in an $	ext{F/S/F}$ trilayer structure using magnetic field control.
model_or_system: The physical system is an all-vdW $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{GeTe}_2$ (ferromagnet) / $	ext{NbSe}_2$ (superconductor) heterostructure. The SDE arises from proximity-induced symmetry breaking and time-reversal symmetry breaking, leading to non-reciprocal supercurrent.
key_observables: Superconducting diode efficiency ($\eta$), non-reciprocal critical current ($\Delta I_c$), and the successful operation of an XNOR logic gate.
important_parameters: Diode efficiency up to 30% at 50 mT; the tunability of diode polarity by the $	ext{F}_3	ext{GeTe}_2$ spin polarization.
main_assumptions: The SDE is enabled by the magnetic proximity effect, which induces necessary symmetry breaking in the superconductor, bypassing the need for a physical weak link junction.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device schematic, $	ext{R-T}$ and $	ext{B}$-field dependence of resistance, $	ext{V-I}$ characteristics showing asymmetry based on premagnetization, and the demonstration of the XNOR logic gate operation.
paper_structure: The paper details the physical setup, characterizes the junction-free SDE using magnetic field protocols to measure non-reciprocity, and culminates in demonstrating the use of this tunable effect for digital logic computation.
why_interesting: This work bridges superconducting physics with solid-state electronics, demonstrating how fundamental quantum phenomena (proximity-induced magnetism) can be harnessed for classical, energy-efficient computing elements.
